chapter_theme: Greatness is not given by birth, rank or wealth. It consists of high aim, self-guarding, doing the rare thing, freedom from conceit and covering others' weakness, and smallness is the same set of features reversed.
structure_note: Parimelazhagar: the excellence of greatness (971), it isn't produced by birth or wealth alone (972-973), how it arises (974), what those who have it do (975), what those without it do (976-977), and both together (978-980).

971.reading: One's radiance is the wealth of aspiration, and one's disgrace is saying 'we will live without it'.
971.nuance: ஒளி and இளி close the previous chapter's last verse (970) and open this one, so the two chapters are stitched together by these words. வெறுக்கை means wealth, so aspiration is presented as a holding. Disgrace lies in the stated resolve to live without it, not in any failure.

972.reading: Birth is alike for all living beings, and distinction is unequal because of the difference in the work they do.
972.nuance: The verse says எல்லா உயிர்க்கும், wider than humanity. செய்தொழில் could be occupation or conduct, and the whole verse's social force depends on that word.

positions.position: Birth is alike only in being embodied through karma; the work that tests greatness itself differs by varna and individual.
Greatness simply can't be recognized by lineage.
All are equal by birth, and difference appears only in the skill shown at one's work.

973.reading: Those who aren't high are not high even when placed high, and those who aren't low are not low even when placed low.
973.nuance: A single word, மேல் or கீழ், names both position and worth, and the verse pries them apart. Pope's couplet takes the position as birth, but Parimelazhagar and Manakkudavar take it as the seat that wealth gives, a high couch against bare ground.

974.reading: Greatness too, like single-minded women, exists only if one holds on to oneself.
974.nuance: The model of masculine greatness is a woman. Conduct expected of wives becomes the standard for great men, a striking move given chapter 91. Parimelazhagar explains self-holding as restraint of mind, speech and body.

975.reading: Those with greatness will accomplish in the right way what is hard to do.
975.nuance: ஆற்றின் adds a limit: the rare deed must be done in the right way. Parimelazhagar adds 'even when poor', which the verse doesn't say. Kalaignar reverses the direction, so that those who do such things are the ones who become great.

976.reading: The aim of cherishing and taking on the great does not exist in the minds of the small.

positions.position: They don't seek to serve the great and acquire their nature, since those proud of birth, wealth or learning think they already have it.
They don't seek to take the great as support, so having great men as allies is itself greatness.

977.reading: Even distinction, should it fall to the unworthy, turns entirely into acts of excess.
977.nuance: Distinction is morally neutral and amplifies whoever has it. Manakkudavar takes சிறப்பு as wealth, while Parimelazhagar takes it as the surplus of birth, wealth and learning.

978.reading: Greatness always bows, and smallness adorns itself in admiration of itself.
978.nuance: பணியும் and அணியும் rhyme, so what looks like opposite motions sound alike. Parimelazhagar reports another reading in which this is a wonder at the way of the world: the high go low and the low go high.

979.reading: Greatness is the absence of pride, and smallness is riding on pride and being done with it.
979.nuance: பெருமிதம், 'pride', shares its root with பெருமை, so the verse defines greatness by the absence of what sounds like its own excess. Manakkudavar marks this as where the chapter turns from negative points to defining greatness.

980.reading: Greatness hides another's weakness, and smallness only tells their faults.
980.nuance: அற்றம் is literally a vulnerable exposure, so this hides a nakedness as much as a fault. Silence, not achievement, finishes the portrait of greatness that opened with high aim.

links.note: 56 gives the wife's self-guarding, தற்காத்து, as what makes a woman. 974 makes the same self-holding the condition of greatness in anyone. A gendered virtue is universalized, and the phrasing reaches back across the book of virtue.

409 uses மேல் and கீழ் of birth, and ranks the unlearned high-born below the learned low-born. 973 uses the same words of position and wealth. Between them, the Kural detaches worth from both axes of hierarchy.

26, in the chapter on renunciants, defines the great as those who do what is hard. 975 repeats that in the book of wealth, with no renunciation. Parimelazhagar himself cites 26 at 971, so this standard crosses from ascetic to householder.
443 calls cherishing the great and making them one's own the rarest of rare things, using the same பேணி. 976 explains why it is rare: the small don't even conceive of it.
595 says a person's height is as great as their will, as a lotus stem rises with the water. 971 calls that will one's wealth and radiance. Both make aspiration the measure of a person.
Consecutive chapters end up in the same place: 980 ends the chapter on greatness with covering faults, and 984 makes not telling others' faults the defining quality of the worthy.

source_issues: 971: no Manakkudavar commentary is aligned to this verse.
974: the Manakkudavar text is marked [#] and nearly identical to Parimelazhagar's gloss, so it may not be independent.
972: Pope renders எல்லா உயிர்க்கும் as 'all men', narrowing the verse in line with Parimelazhagar's மக்களுயிர்.
973: Pope's couplet uses 'lofty line' and 'lowly birth', while the commentators take the position as wealth or seat.
977: Manakkudavar's text appears corrupt at நிதியை இறப்பாரிடத்தே பொருந்தின்.
